flows.name: A personal agent signs in to a website (1Password for Agents)
flows.summary: For an individual or family account: a person delegates a task that needs a sign-in, such as booking a flight, and 1Password fills the login in the agent's browser instead of the person sharing the password with the agent. Opt-in, for supported agent apps.

steps.what: Connects 1Password to a supported agent app. Connecting lets the agent ask 1Password to sign in; it does not give the agent access to the person's vaults.
Reaches a step of its task that needs a sign-in and asks 1Password to sign in.
steps.agent: Carries out the delegated task (for example booking a flight or shopping for groceries) and asks 1Password for a sign-in when it needs one.

steps.what: Shows the person which agent is asking to sign in, with suggested logins for the website.
Reviews the request and chooses whether to approve it.
Fills the username, password and one-time password directly into the website's sign-in form in the agent's browser; the agent app makes sure the agent cannot see the sign-in page.
Continues the task, signed in. The person can disconnect the integration at any time.
steps.agent: Completes the task without the credentials entering its chat.

flows.name: An AI agent in a browser gets a credential (Secure Agentic Autofill, with Browserbase)
flows.summary: 1Password's first implementation for browser-use agents, through Browserbase: credentials are injected into the agent's browser by the 1Password browser extension only when required and always authorised by a person, so the agent and the underlying model never see them.

steps.what: Sets it up: 1Password shows a prompt that details what the agentic browser will be able to request from 1Password; Browserbase cannot access, see or modify anything in a vault without approval.
Runs a workflow in the browser and, when it needs to sign in, informs 1Password that a credential is being requested.
steps.agent: Executes the browser workflow and requests a credential from 1Password instead of receiving one in its prompt.

steps.what: Identifies the appropriate credentials and asks the person for approval; where a site has more than one login, the person chooses which to use.
Approves or refuses in real time; every credential request needs a person's approval by default.

If, and only if, the person approves, injects the credential into the browser over an end-to-end encrypted channel (a protocol built on the Noise Framework) between the approving 1Password device and the extension in the remote browser, just in time.
Carries on with the workflow, signed in; the credential never enters the model's context.
steps.agent: Completes the workflow with access limited to the credentials that workflow needs (least privilege).
